status: Open to contributions and expert-agent review; maintainer @Mister-Meeseeks. A passing checker is not acceptance: promotion to a new frontier version is a maintainer decision.

tracks.useful_outcome: Lower verified symbolic fill on a drawn matrix, starting from its inherited order

tasks.question: Can you find an elimination order for the drawn matrix with fewer symbolic Cholesky factor nonzeros (ties broken by the squared column sum) than its current frontier order?
methods: Local search from the inherited order with tools/contribute.py and your session seed
Seeded METIS nested-dissection restarts, then local refinement
Swap and block-move neighbourhoods on the elimination tree or supernodes
Annealing or tabu search with a declared evaluation budget
tasks.acceptance_gate: tools/verify_submission.py reports verified and improves_current_frontier; the PR carries one sparse-submission/v1 certificate under submissions/, the full trace, seed and budget. Promotion is the maintainer's decision.

first_step.expected: PASS bcsstk08 (v002): factor nonzeros 30645, squared column sum 1730951, max column 106
first_step.scope: Positive control on one row; the picker gives the drawn row's own check.

tasks.first_experiment: Rerun the starter search on the drawn matrix with your session seed (not the README's example seed 2301), then try one different neighbourhood under the same evaluation budget.
allowed_variations: Any search method, if its budget and trace are recorded
Any matrix in the current frontier version
scope_change_triggers: A change to the objective, the inputs or the checker

existing_checks.scope: Author-run donor rehearsal improved six matrices from v001 to v002 (seed 2301, 2048 proposals each)
existing_checks.remaining: The other 22 matrices have not had a search from their v002 orders; rerunning seed 2301 is not new work.

tracks.useful_outcome: Evidence on which search methods work on which matrix families, under equal budgets

tasks.question: Under one fixed evaluation budget per matrix, does a different search method (or a selector between METIS restarts and local search) beat the starter optimizer across both empirical families and the synthetic ones?
methods: Equal-budget comparison against tools/contribute.py on at least eight matrices spanning every family
A portfolio that chooses between METIS restarts and local search from cheap matrix features
tasks.acceptance_gate: Every compared order verifies; the report gives the budget, seeds, per-matrix results including losses, and fixes the matrix set before running. Any new frontier orders are submitted separately as certificates.

first_step.expected: "verified": true and "instances": 28 in the JSON output

tasks.first_experiment: Pick eight matrices covering all six families before running anything, then compare two methods at 2048 evaluations each with two seeds.
allowed_variations: Budget size, if equal across methods
Which matrices, if chosen before running
scope_change_triggers: Held-out matrices or a new benchmark

tracks.useful_outcome: Independent checks of the scorer, the submission checker and contributed certificates

tasks.question: Does the symbolic scorer compute factor nonzeros correctly, and does the submission checker reject every malformed or forged certificate?
methods: An independently written symbolic factorization (elimination tree and column counts) compared on every frontier order
Adversarial certificates: wrong hashes, invalid permutations, forged scores, oversized input
tasks.acceptance_gate: A report under research/<session>/ with the independent code, commands and outputs; any false acceptance gets a failing test. Don't weaken the checker to accept a candidate.
tasks.first_experiment: Recompute the scores of all 28 v002 orders with your own column-count code and compare.
scope_change_triggers: A scorer disagreement (report it at once, don't patch around it)

tasks.question: Does an open ordering PR's certificate verify from a clean checkout of main, and does it improve the current frontier?
methods: Rerun tools/verify_submission.py on the PR's certificate from main, following the hub's verify playbook
tasks.acceptance_gate: A verification note on the PR with the command, its output and the commit checked; a passing check isn't acceptance.

first_step.expected: PASS 685_bus (v002): factor nonzeros 3618, squared column sum 24490, max column 16

tracks.useful_outcome: A controlled answer to whether lower symbolic fill lowers real factorization time or memory

tasks.question: On a stated machine, does the frontier order make CHOLMOD factorization of the drawn matrix faster or smaller than the AMD and METIS orders, once ordering time and repeated factorizations are counted?
methods: Repeated CHOLMOD factorizations with randomized order and warm-up, reporting medians and spread
Peak memory and factor size from CHOLMOD's own statistics
tasks.acceptance_gate: A benchmark report under research/<session>/ naming the hardware, CHOLMOD version and settings, baselines, ordering time, number of repeats, and numerical residuals; no ranking claim from one machine.
tasks.first_experiment: Time 30 factorizations each of the frontier, AMD and METIS orders on bcsstk08 and 1138_bus, interleaved.
allowed_variations: Other sparse Cholesky libraries, if pinned
scope_change_triggers: A proposal to change the objective to a runtime measure

tasks.question: Which public, redistributable matrix family would most strengthen the benchmark, and does it qualify under the project's input rules?
methods: Propose a family with source, license, hashes and why it matters, before any search on it
tasks.acceptance_gate: A proposal issue (research template) with source URLs, terms, SHA-256 hashes and a qualification run; adding inputs is a maintainer decision.

first_step.expected: All required external inputs match frozen hashes. Upstream terms still apply.
